title: On the gauge-invariant orbital angular momentum of vector optical vortices in the paraxial approximation and beyond
authors: E. V. Maliutina, E. A. Vashukevich, V. A. Leonov, D. D. Reshetnikov, T. Yu. Golubeva
abstract: In this paper we present a gauge-invariant formalism for describing the spin and orbital angular momenta of scalar and vector optical vortices. The correction term, arising from consistent incorporation of the transverse vector potential's nonlocality, restores gauge invariance and makes it possible to separate the total angular momentum into spin and orbital components. We propose a method for calculating the orbital and spin angular momenta of multimode vector vortex fields and show that the orbital angular momentum of such beams contains two qualitatively different components. The polarization-independent contribution to the orbital angular momentum is related to the topological charge that determines the order of the phase singularity, while the polarization-dependent one is proportional to the helical topological charge that determines the spatial inhomogeneity of the polarization. We also discuss the quantization procedure for fields with spatially inhomogeneous polarization in terms of modes with a helical topological charge, and examine the limits of applicability of the proposed formalism.
summary: This paper introduces a gauge-invariant framework to calculate the orbital and spin angular momenta of vector optical vortices. It successfully separates the total angular momentum into two distinct components: one related to the phase structure and another related to the polarization inhomogeneity. This advancement is crucial for accurately modeling light beams beyond the simple paraxial approximation.
main_problem: The paper develops a gauge-invariant formalism to accurately describe the spin and orbital angular momenta (OAM) of both scalar and vector optical vortices, especially beyond the paraxial approximation.
main_result: The OAM of vector vortices is shown to have two distinct physical contributions: one related to the phase singularity (polarization-independent) and another proportional to the helical topological charge (polarization-dependent).
method: The authors construct gauge-invariant quantities by incorporating non-local corrections to the vector potential, solving related Poisson equations in Fourier space, and employing Borel regularization for divergent asymptotic series.
model_or_system: The system under study is vector optical vortices, characterized by a vector potential A, which can be analyzed for arbitrary multimode fields with spatially inhomogeneous polarization.
key_observables: Gauge-invariant Orbital Angular Momentum ($\mathcal{L}_{inv}$), Spin Angular Momentum ($\mathcal{S}_{inv}$), and the total angular momentum ($\mathcal{J}_{inv}$).
important_parameters: Topological charge ($l$), Helicity ($\sigma$), and the helical topological charge ($w$). The nonparaxiality parameter $\xi$ is also crucial.
main_assumptions: The formalism requires careful handling of gauge invariance, and the derived series expansions are asymptotic, necessitating Borel regularization for physical interpretation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the need for gauge invariance in angular momentum calculations, deriving the gauge-invariant potentials, and then applying this formalism to separate the OAM into polarization-independent and polarization-dependent components for multimode fields.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to quantify angular momentum in complex light fields, which is fundamental for understanding light-matter interactions and quantum state manipulation in quantum optics.
